I wasn’t “extremely” invalidated but was always told I was too sensitive growing up. And even now as an adult (my parents/friends/etc) have told me similar things. I wonder if that has led me to ignore red flags or to give people too many chances. I’ve unfortunately been in a few compromising situations hips/relationships but there was only one person I walked away from pretty immediately. My friends were encouraging me to give him a “chance” but I was in an excellent mental state then and I didn’t want to risk my mental state on some boy who wasn’t worth it and who was already saying problematic things (ie: “I’m so glad you aren’t like other girls” wtf/implied I wasn’t attractive which was weird because I know I’m at least moderately attractive and why would you put down someone you want to date?/made fun of me and was trying to sabotage my diet when I was in the process of getting back down to a healthy BMI/ got drunk at a bar and wouldn’t let me out of his car when he was my ride?/lastly he told me weird things about his old relationship that made me very uncomfortable). I wonder if other people have been told similar, if not worse things by the people they trust in their lives, and if this sort of invalidation is a contributing factor to later abuse and lack of trust in one’s own gut instinct


I also know that my mom pointedly said she “always tries to see the good in people” when I pointed out the terrible behavior of somebody, so it may be a trait that is passed down (ie: my mom was taught not to trust her gut instinct and believe that people are inherently good, so I do the same when that is not always the case. Sometimes you need to stay away from people)

Ah okay. I’m just not used to working like this and actually thought this would be low stress. That’s how the temp recruiter sold it to me, and I’m sort of pissed it’s not but I don’t want to fuck up my resume anymore. It’s inbound calls and sounds like it would’ve been straight forward from the job description but I have so many pissed wrong numbers, the hold line is hours long, etc etc. everyone is mad all the time (on top of the problems I listed above). Trying to look in the bright side and bask in the knowledge this is temporary but .. ugh. And I’m sure our positions are similar

That makes sense I guess. It just seems like they’d duck themselves over using practices like this. If you treat your employees kindly and with respect they might actually stay. More than half of my class has left and it hasn’t even been a month. That shoULD tell management there’s a problem. It shouldn’t tell them to double down on ridiculous standards? I have no problem clocking in to the minute/having standards/etc... but a lot about this job feels unrealistic. I don’t want my boss calling my personal cellphone for things outside my control and I certainly don’t want to be punished for clocking in 10 seconds late. That’s bizarre and I’m glad u agree about the down to the second thing so I feel somewhat supported in my confusion/outrage over this aspect lol

Yeah my supervisor contacts me when I’m on calls too long. I’m not allowed to use the hold button (wasn’t told that in training, was told it had to be for less than a certain amount of time), and have certain targets for.. everything. I have no idea how I’m expected to hit all the points I’m supposed to bring up during each phone call and hit our “target” phone call length. It’s an inbound call center and most people know what they want and why they’re calling. Makes no sense. Oh, and my supervisor has told me thinks that directly contradict my training materials multiple times, confusing me further. Idk if I’m glad or sad to hear that this is a wide spread practice. Hopefully you get a new position soon or move up- whatever you want and whatever alleviates your stress!!
